decisions.issues: Minor only. The right side of the moustache droops down toward the sand instead of curling up, which reads as wet hair pressed flat, not a beard. The cheek and jaw are clean and the chin is pressed into the sand. The shoulder and back mass is soft but reads as a man lying face down. The rope loops on the torso sit on the shoulder and ribs, well clear of the neck, which matches 1.2. The caption fits over the grey sky and distant surf at the top left, clear of the face.

v06 is acceptable, with minor drift only. It is an edit of v03 that fixes the setting. The stone walls, sea, boats and hilltop fort are gone. It is now the mud-plastered, palm-thatched hut, and the open doorway shows palms and wet paddy in grey rain, which matches the 6.2 v07 and 6.4 v07 picks. The beat reads. The Fisherman (grizzled grey beard, cream vest, red lungi) crouches by the mat, looking down and speaking low. His right hand crosses his chest to adjust the white cloth on his own LEFT shoulder, and his hands are sound. Nagoji half-sits on the mat looking up at him. Nagoji matches the sheet and the chapter 4 row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with light stubble, small gold ear stud, long loose curly hair, bare chest, cream dhoti and bandaged wrists, with no irons. The rope burns on his chest are reddish welts, not blood. Both his hands are anatomically sound, and the brand is not shown. There are no painted balloons, text or pseudo-text; the brass pot has only a faint floral chasing, no letters. The lamp has an open wick with no glass. Lettering space: the thatch band across the top left (x 0.0 to 0.5, y 0.0 to 0.18), the plain mud wall between the two heads (x 0.38 to 0.52, y 0.18 to 0.42), and the sky above the palms at top right (x 0.82 to 1.0, y 0.05 to 0.35). The long caption can sit along the top band or the bottom-left mat (x 0.0 to 0.5, y 0.88 to 1.0). Minor drift: (1) the red lungi has a faint check weave, whereas the script asks for plain dyed colour and the 6.2 and 6.4 lungis are plain; (2) the palette is warmer and sharper than 6.2; (3) the bandages cover only his wrists here, while 6.4 v07 wraps the whole hands.

Acceptable, with notes. v06 is the v05 composition with the brand added, and it fixes the one gap v05 had: the brand now shows. Brand: a pale, puckered patch of raised ridges on the forearm he holds out to the Woman, which is his LEFT, about a hand's width above the wrist. It has no numerals and is not a cross. Its three ridge-strokes suggest letterforms (roughly 'L-c-u' when zoomed). At 1:1 and at print size they read as a burned-letter scar, not a word. This is the same level of letter suggestion as the scrolled monogram accepted in 5.4 v02, but the two shapes differ. The arm is turned so the brand sits more on the upper or thumb side than clearly on the inner side. The light is warm hearth light rather than 'cool'. There is a faint shadow under Nagoji's lower lip, within 'light stubble at most'. Everything else matches the beat. The interior is dim, with hearth smoke rising into the lit hole in the thatch. The ochre tunic lies peeled off in a pile on the woven mat. He wears the cream dhoti, and red rope burns cross his bare chest with no blood. The Woman has a grey-streaked low knot and undyed cotton over both shoulders, with no blouse and no gold. She washes his arm over a clay basin with his fingers hidden in her wet cloth, her mouth pulled tight. The Fisherman, in red lungi and shoulder cloth, squats at the mat's edge. Nagoji is on model: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear drop, no irons. Anatomy and hands are sound. No painted text, balloons or boxes. Lettering: the FISHERMAN balloon fits on the plain mud wall at upper left, beside and above his head. The NAGOJI balloon fits in the dark roof beams at top centre, between his hair and the smoke column. Both read left to right in script order.

Minor only. The wreck sits beached at the left edge instead of offshore on the reef (per 2.4), so it does not match its offshore position in 3.3. Nagoji's left foot has bandaged toes, which the script does not call for. The Young Fisherman's vest is deep indigo rather than faded blue. Nagoji is on-model: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, open ochre tunic, rope burns on his chest, no rope. Both fishermen are on the correct sides and doing the right actions, and the forearm mark is not yet readable. There is no text. Lettering space: sky top-left above the wreck for the Young Fisherman's line, and sky between Nagoji's and the Fisherman's heads for 'Look at this.'

Clean. This is a real tight insert, not a crop. The brand on the inner forearm, above the soaked wrist bandage, is a puckered patch of ridged scar tissue with no legible letters, numerals or cross, and no blood. The Fisherman's sandy thumb is scraping wet sand at the left edge. The ochre tunic, cream dhoti and grey surf behind match 3.1. No lettering needed.

Minor only. The Wary Fisherman stands closer to shin-deep in the surf than ankle-deep at the tide line. The wreck is offshore on the right, where 3.1 had it beached on the left. He matches his 2.1/2.4 design (gaunt, long grey-streaked beard, dark brown vest, off-white lungi, net coil on his shoulder), stands alone, and glances up the coast toward the wreck. Hands and legs are sound, with no text. The large open sky top-left and centre holds the caption and both balloons.

Acceptable, with minor drift only. (1) The edit did not remove the small gold ear stud from the Fisherman, and the Young Fisherman also wears a gold drop at the ear. Both are tiny at page scale, and both men are clearly not Nagoji (grey beard; headband and chin beard). (2) The Wary Fisherman is a few paces off, but his head turns back toward the group rather than toward the palms. (3) Nagoji's hands are unbandaged, as in the earlier accepted takes. Everything else is clean. The flat grey storm sky and heaving grey-green surf now match page 3. The wreck is one high-sided dark hull with a carved stern castle and a snapped leaning mast. Nagoji is up on his right forearm with a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, the gold stud, the torn ochre tunic, the cream dhoti and no irons. The brand on his LEFT forearm is pale raised wavy ridges with no letters, numerals or cross. The Fisherman crouches in a red lungi, cream vest and shoulder cloth. The Young Fisherman stands in an indigo lungi and headband, and the Wary Fisherman stands off with an off-white lungi and net. Hands are sound, there is no text and there are no painted boxes. Open grey sky in the upper centre (between the wreck and the Young Fisherman) and along the top-left holds Nagoji's balloon clear of every face.

Acceptable, with minor drift only. (1) The Fisherman points south with his whole arm instead of jerking his chin; the beat still reads. (2) A few fishing huts and beached boats appear along the distant shore. They are period-appropriate. Everything else is clean. The relight worked: flat grey overcast, grey-green foaming surf and wet dark sand match 4.1. The Fisherman matches 4.1: grizzled grey beard, thick moustache, curly hair, cream vest, white cloth on his shoulder, red lungi, and no ear stud. Nagoji appears only from behind at the left edge (ochre rags, gold stud, light jaw stubble), which is allowed. The pointing hand is well formed, there is no text and there are no painted boxes. The palm line runs away into haze as scripted. The wide open sky across the right two-thirds easily holds all three Fisherman balloons clear of both heads.

Acceptable, with minor drift only. (1) Nagoji sits upright with one knee raised and his left arm resting on it, rather than propped on one elbow as in 4.1 and 4.4. In a close shot this is a small continuity slip. (2) The brand shows on the upper/outer side of the LEFT forearm rather than the inner side. It is a patch of pale, raised, looping cord-like ridges, blurred past reading, with no legible letters, no numerals and no cross. The loops lean slightly script-like when zoomed, but they read as scar tissue at panel size. Everything else is clean. The relight now matches the page: grey overcast, grey-green foaming surf. The face matches the sheet, with a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin with only a stubble shadow, the small gold ear stud and long loose curls. He wears the torn ochre tunic over rope-burn lines and the cream dhoti. His waking, alert upward gaze fits the beat. Hands are sound, there is no text and there are no painted boxes. Open grey sky in the upper right holds the caption and his one-word balloon clear of the face.

Acceptable, with minor drift only. (1) The wreck at right is a skeletal hulk with standing masts and tattered sail, not the carved-stern high-sided hull now shown in 4.1. It is small and at the frame edge. (2) The brand on Nagoji's LEFT forearm is a small pale ring-and-swirl mark on the upper side of the arm, rounder than the ridged patch in 4.1 and 4.3. It has no letters, no numerals and no cross, and it is tiny at page scale. (3) The Fisherman's raised brows are subtle, though his wide eyes and parted lips read as surprise. Everything else is clean. The relight matches 4.1 to 4.3 (grey overcast, grey-green surf, wet sand). The Fisherman matches 4.1 and 4.2: grey curls and beard, cream vest, shoulder cloth, checked red lungi, no ear stud. Nagoji is propped on his right forearm with chin lifted and shoulders squared. He has the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin with only a stubble shadow, the gold stud, the torn ochre tunic and cream dhoti, and no irons. Hands are sound, there is no text and there are no painted boxes. The wide open sky across the top holds all three balloons above both heads.

Acceptable, with minor drift only. (1) Nagoji's dangling near arm (his RIGHT) has a small reddish mottled scrape mid-forearm. It reads as a fresh abrasion, not gore, but an attentive reader could take it for the brand on the wrong arm. (2) The Young Fisherman here has a moustache, a gold ear drop and a sleeveless indigo tunic. In 4.1 he wears a chin beard and a blue vest. (3) The wreck shows standing masts and a tattered sail, unlike the carved-stern hull of 4.1. (4) The party walks right toward the wreck, a mild direction flip from 4.1's palms. The beat is complete. The grinning Fisherman (white teeth, grey beard, cream vest, shoulder cloth, red lungi) holds Nagoji under the shoulders from behind. The Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, headband) holds his legs at the knee and ankle. The Wary Fisherman (off-white lungi, brown vest, net, long grey beard) walks ahead scanning the shore. A sand crab sidles in the lower-left foreground. Nagoji has the moustache, a clean-shaven chin with only stubble, the gold stud and no irons, manacles, chain or collar. The relight matches the page's grey overcast. Hands and feet are sound, there is no text and there are no painted boxes. Open sky at top centre, between the Fisherman's head and the Young Fisherman's head, holds both balloons clear of every face.
